papers.title: Learning from What You Retrieve: Online RL Fine-Tuning for Semantic Retrieval
papers.summary: In large-scale e-commerce retrieval, dual-encoder retrievers are optimized for contrastive similarity, whereas downstream rerankers capture finer-grained relevance preferences; this objective mismatch limits end-to-end retrieval quality. Reinforcement Learning offers a way to use reward-model feedback for retriever adaptation, but we observe that standard policy-gradient updates can degrade embedding geometry, especially when the document index must remain frozen due to industrial constraints. papers.title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: A Statistical Perspective
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has emerged as a central framework for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. Despite its practical success, RLHF raises fundamental statistical questions because it relies on noisy, subjective, and heterogeneous feedback to learn reward models and optimize policies. This review provides a statistical perspective on RLHF, focusing primarily on LLM alignment. papers.title: EVOL: Simulator-Guided Evolutionary Expert Synthesis for Deployment-Free Learning Path Recommendation
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) for learning path recommendation (LPR) faces two coupled obstacles. First, the policy must commit to a sequence of L concepts without intermediate feedback, producing a combinatorial search space that grows super-exponentially with L and provides reward only at the final step. papers.title: Graph-GRPO: Dependency-Aware Credit Assignment for Generative E-commerce Search Relevance
papers.summary: Search relevance modeling is a core task in e-commerce search systems, assessing how well a user query matches candidate products. Rather than relying on a single holistic matching signal, relevance judgment often requires structured reasoning over query understanding, product understanding, and facet-level matching. With large language models (LLMs), this process is increasingly formulated as chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and optimized with reinforcement learning (RL). papers.title: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Formulaic Alpha Factor Generation and Adaptive Composition
papers.summary: Alpha factor mining aims to automatically construct predictive signals from raw market features and is fundamental to stock return forecasting. Recent reinforcement learning (RL) approaches formulate formulaic alpha discovery as a sequential decision problem yet face three key challenges. papers.title: Reinforcement learning enables autonomous microrobot navigation and intervention in simulated blood capillaries
papers.summary: Abstract Autonomous microrobots navigating biological vasculature could enable targeted drug delivery and thrombolysis, yet training control policies for physiologically complex environments remains an open challenge. Prior reinforcement learning (RL) studies of microrobotic navigation have largely used idealized geometries lacking realistic flow in confined branching, and dense cellular obstacles. papers.summary: Abstract Applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to economic modeling reveals a fundamental tension: standard RL agents do not behave as competitive price-takers. While macroeconomic models typically assume agents take aggregate conditions as given, a naive single-agent RL algorithm learns to internalize its impact on the environment, effectively exerting market power. papers.title: ViSalRec: Visual and Saliency-Informed Reward Augmentation for Sequential Recommender Systems
papers.summary: In Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based sequential recommendation, offline training often reduces user feedback to sparse binary rewards, weakening credit assignment and limiting policy optimisation. In visual recommendation settings, user choices are also shaped by product appearance, visual attention, and semantic impressions, which provide preference cues that binary outcomes cannot capture. papers.title: POLAR: Policy Optimization through Larger Reasoners
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is a practical way to improve the reasoning and decision-making abilities of large language models, but its training signal is often sparse. When a policy faces prompts beyond its current ability, every sampled trajectory in a group may fail the verifier, resulting in an all-zero group. papers.summary: Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) experiences are difficult to share with the public because they are essentially processes that rely on physical interactions with embodied, tacit, and situated phenomena in specific cultural contexts. papers.summary: Pharmacies operate under constant pressure to deliver safe, timely, and cost-effective services while maintaining strict regulatory compliance and resilient supply chains. Manual, repetitive back-office work—such as purchase order creation, invoice matching, stock reconciliation, expiry tracking, and dispensing documentation—consumes significant pharmacist time and is prone to error. papers.summary: Collaborative robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and edge inference nodes inside Industrial Control Systems (ICS) now let AI models drive physical actuators. Robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) with cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) may improve target localization and parenchymal sampling. papers.summary: Spectral 3D computer vision combines wavelength-resolved measurements with geometric information to support material-aware reconstruction, perception, and scene analysis. However, the literature remains fragmented across hyperspectral and multispectral sensing, cross-spectral depth and pose estimation, spectral point clouds, LiDAR–hyperspectral fusion, and neural scene representations. papers.title: Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL
papers.summary: Generative retrieval offers a promising alternative by unifying the multi-stage retrieval process into a single end-to-end model. However, its practical adoption in industrial e-commerce search remains challenging, given the massive and dynamic product catalogs, strict latency requirements, and the need to align retrieval with downstream ranking goals. papers.title: Label-free Industrial Fault Detection via Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning: A System for Run-to-Failure Prognostics
papers.summary: Machinery fault detection (MFD) remains heavily reliant on supervised learning, which struggles with the scarcity of fault labels in real-world settings. While reinforcement learning (RL) offers a framework to model the sequential nature of degradation, current ''RL-based'' MFD methods reduce the problem to a static contextual bandit (CB) formulation: by ignoring state transitions and discarding the temporal discount factor, they collapse to standard supervised classification. papers.title: Learning from Unreachable Rewards: Hint-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning for Generative Recommendation
papers.summary: Semantic-ID generative recommenders represent each item as a short sequence of discrete semantic tokens and predict the next item by autoregressively generating this token sequence. This paradigm enables a unified generation interface for item IDs, histories, and item text, but it also creates a structured optimization bottleneck during reward-based post-training: when an early semantic token enters the wrong branch of the item-token space, finite rollout groups rarely reach the ground-truth item, so group-relative optimization receives identical zero rewards and produces no useful advantage.

papers.summary: Embedding-based retrieval (EBR) is a prevailing method in modern e-commerce search, retrieving relevant items from billions of candidates in response to users' queries. While recent methods often fine-tune large language models (LLMs) for representation learning, they typically lack robust mechanisms for handling complex and implicit semantics.
